extra.message: User-controlled `post_id` is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to conn.execute(): `'SELECT * FROM posts WHERE id = '+post_id`. The weak regex guard `^\d+$` uses re.M (multiline) which allows newline-injected payloads to bypass it (e.g. `1\nDROP...`), enabling SQL injection.

Multiple SQL queries build the WHERE clause from the `username` variable using string concatenation, str.format(), %-formatting, and f-strings, then pass the result to cursor.execute(). Any of these allow SQL injection because user input is interpolated directly into the SQL statement instead of using parameterized queries.

The `url` parameter from request.args is passed to urllib.request.urlopen() and the response body is returned to the client. The only guard is `url.startswith('https://insecurewebapp.com')`, which is trivially bypassable (e.g. `https://insecurewebapp.com@attacker.com/`, or a redirect from that host) allowing Server-Side Request Forgery against internal resources.

The HTTP request path (self.path) is appended to the current working directory (`path += self.path`) and the resulting file is opened and returned to the client without proper sanitization. The regex guard `r'/\.\.\/\.\.\/'` only matches a single specific leading pattern and fails to block traversal sequences (e.g. `/../`, URL-encoded `%2e%2e`, or paths not at the start), allowing path traversal and arbitrary local file disclosure (LFI).

extra.message: The server reads the `username` cookie from the HTTP request and deserializes it via pickle (Username.pickle() / pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(cookie))) without any signature or integrity check. Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data leads to arbitrary code execution (RCE). See exploitApickle.py for a working RCE payload generator targeting this sink.

The `username` value is written into the HTML response with `"

Hello %s

" % username` without any HTML escaping. When derived from request-controlled data this produces reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

The `username` value decrypted from the attacker-controlled `session_id` cookie is written directly into the HTML response via `"Hello %s" % username` with no HTML output encoding, resulting in reflected/stored Cross-Site Scripting.

The session_id cookie is decrypted with AES in CBC mode (AES.MODE_CBC) using an IV taken from the ciphertext and with no authentication/MAC. Unauthenticated CBC decryption of user-supplied data is vulnerable to padding-oracle and bit-flipping/tampering attacks, allowing forgery/manipulation of the session value.

extra.message: Payment signatures are computed as sha256(secret + payment_information) instead of using HMAC. The secret-prefix MAC construction over SHA-256 is vulnerable to a length-extension attack, allowing an attacker to append data (e.g. a higher amount) and forge a valid signature without knowing the secret.

TLS certificate hostname verification is disabled (context.check_hostname = False) and the Host header is built via string interpolation. Disabling check_hostname permits man-in-the-middle attacks, and unvalidated Host header construction enables HTTP header/host header injection.

Class defines __reduce__ returning (os.system, (cmd,)) so that unpickling executes an OS command (reverse shell). This demonstrates the insecure-deserialization sink and is the danger that pickle.loads on untrusted input exposes (arbitrary command execution).
